Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/f1c18d26fb7b6f1969bcda14d71ac18429466b4be8847097f227cdc537fdc8d9.png) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/4b752e33d4ca3154590a5dc16ec3addd1d45a9618c92283903ff33d3818b8266.png)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/d10e552c42ff8fe0df517b6297582bd5eeefdf29896a51005c79bd399a363c13.png)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)=y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)=x, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2})=0,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})=2y, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\frac{y}{x},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/8c2cef2ba5322cc545860caa4d2f503f5f48a3374cce7c0f1e910a56f0357a64.png)
Thus, the missing entries are $y,\:$ $0,\:$ and $\ln{x}.$
